findings_qualitative.value: JVLA 7 mm image resolves azimuthally highly asymmetric knotty dust emission near the inner edge of the outer ring

evidence.quote: Intriguingly, the Q band image resolved the azimuthally highly asymmetric, knotty dust emission sources close to the inner edge of the outer ring.

findings_qualitative.value: Q-band knots are more likely dust than free-free emission

evidence.quote: In other words, the $>$3-$\sigma$ sources in our Q-fiducial image more likely trace dust emission instead of free-free emission.

findings_qualitative.value: DM Tau cannot be optically thin at 225 GHz

evidence.quote: Conversely, the large contrast between the morphology resolved at 225 GHz and 40-48 GHz means that DM Tau cannot be optically thin at 225 GHz.

claims.hypothesis: Is the outer dust ring of DM Tau azimuthally asymmetric at 7 mm?
claims.experiment: High-resolution JVLA Q-band imaging combined from several epochs and configurations, plus visibility moment analysis
claims.result: Knots at ~3-6 sigma in the east to south of the ~25 au ring; brightest knot at least 100% brighter than the opposite side; weak dipole signal
claims.finding: The ring is highly asymmetric and knotty at 40-48 GHz while only weakly asymmetric at 225 GHz

evidence.quote: Intriguingly, the Q band image resolved the azimuthally highly asymmetric, knotty dust emission sources close to the inner edge of the outer ring.
Higher sensitivity data will robustly confirm the presence of asymmetry.

claims.hypothesis: Do the knots and the rest of the ring host different maximum grain sizes?
claims.experiment: Two-dust-plus-free-free unresolved SED model fitted to 8-700 GHz flux densities with emcee
claims.result: Grown dust a_max ~0.3 mm; small dust a_max below 100 um (best fit 0.055 mm)
claims.finding: a_max is likely at least 300 um in the knots and at most 50 um in the rest of the ring

evidence.quote: the maximum grain size ($a_{\mbox{\scriptsize max}}$) in these knotty dust emission sources is likely $\gtrsim$300 $\mu$m, whereas it is $\lesssim$50 $\mu$m in the rest of the ring

claims.hypothesis: Are the 40-48 GHz knots free-free emission rather than dust?
claims.experiment: Compared Q-band knots with the X and Ku band free-free images and scaled intensities
claims.result: Free-free knots are at most ~30 uJy/beam and mostly inside the cavity, while knots are 50-70 uJy/beam and tied to the ring
claims.finding: The >3 sigma Q-band knots are most likely dust emission

evidence.quote: Conversely, the $>$3-$\sigma$ detected 40–48 GHz knots in the Q-fiducial image that are closely associated with the brightest 225 GHz ring are most likely dust emission sources.

claims.hypothesis: What produces the azimuthal asymmetry and dust concentration?
claims.experiment: Discussion of the grain growth, trapping, planet-disk interaction and vortex scenarios in light of the SED and images
claims.result: Grown dust is found at the inner edge of the ring
claims.finding: Trapping of inward-migrating grown dust is proposed but the mechanism is not identified

evidence.quote: The exact mechanism for developing the azimuthal asymmetry has not yet been identified, which may be due to planet-disk interaction that might also be responsible for the creation of the dust cavity and pressure bump.

claims.hypothesis: Does apparent symmetry of transitional disks depend on optical depth at the observing frequency?
claims.experiment: Compared DM Tau morphology at 225 GHz and 40-48 GHz
claims.result: Weak asymmetry at 225 GHz and strong asymmetry at 40-48 GHz
claims.finding: Asymmetry is difficult to diagnose at 225 GHz or above owing to high optical depth

evidence.quote: In other words, the apparent symmetric or asymmetric morphology of the transitional disks may be related to the optical depths of those disks at the observing frequency.

limitations_admitted.value: Dipole moments could not be robustly fitted owing to noise

limitations_admitted.value: Free-free parameters barely constrained owing to variability

evidence.quote: As a consequence of the poorly constrained variability, the free parameters of the free-free emission components were barely constrained

limitations_admitted.value: Dust masses are upper limits for the assumed DSHARP opacities

evidence.quote: Our dust mass estimates may be regarded upper limits, since the default DSHARP dust are not as opaque as those that included graphitic carbons

referee_caveats_inferred: ALMA flux densities are taken from heterogeneous archival data with no stated reduction or flux-scale uncertainty, and the SED is non-simultaneous across 2010-2019 for a variable source
Two-component model is weakly constrained and results depend on hand-set likelihood constraints and artificial uncertainties for X and Ku bands
Asymmetry significance relies on ~3-6 sigma knots and a visibility test with positively biased noise
Spatial association of grown dust with knots is inferred, not fitted
